name: The division of Śaivism into Atimārga and Mantramārga
members: Atimārga (Pāśupata, Lākula; later also Kālāmukha/Kāpālika in scholarly schemes)
Mantramārga (Siddhānta; Bhairava tantras — Mantrapīṭha and Vidyāpīṭha; Vāma; Gāruḍa; Bhūta)

relations.note: the Mantramārga's dual goal marks it off from the Atimārga

notes: U17 owns the Atimārga's own account (lin:atimarga). The 'householder vs ascetic' contrast follows scholarly synthesis (Sanderson) of the texts and is to be checked against the Niśvāsamukha in Phase D.

definitions.definition: The Mantramārga's scriptures rank the Atimārga (the ascetic Pāśupata and Lākula paths, for liberation alone) below the Mantramārga, whose initiates may seek powers and enjoyments as well as liberation, and which is open to householders.

name: The fivefold hierarchy of religion (laukika, vaidika, ādhyātmika, atimārga, mantra)

definitions.definition: Religious teaching is graded as worldly, Vedic, spiritual (Sāṃkhya-Yoga), Atimārga and Mantra; in the Kāmika each is spoken by one of Sadāśiva's five faces, each fivefold, making twenty-five streams.

name: The five streams (srotas) of Śaiva revelation

definitions.definition: The Mantra-tantras issue from Sadāśiva's five faces: Siddhānta from the upper (Īśāna), Gāruḍa from the east, Vāma from the north, Bhūta from the west (Sadyojāta) and Bhairava from the south.

name: Mantrapīṭha and Vidyāpīṭha
notes: The Kāmika says only that the Bhairava tantra is 'twofold'; the names Mantrapīṭha/Vidyāpīṭha are from other scriptures (e.g. Jayadrathayāmala) and scholarly synthesis.

definitions.definition: The twofold Bhairava tantra of the southern face (Kāmika: 'twofold'): the Mantrapīṭha centred on male Bhairava forms such as Svacchanda, and the Vidyāpīṭha centred on goddesses and feminine mantras, subdivided into Yāmala and Śakti tantras.

name: The twenty-eight Śaiva Siddhānta Āgamas (mūlāgamas)
notes: Member order is the Kāmika's. Variant lists: the Kiraṇa has Nārasiṃha (= Sarvokta slot), Bhadra (= Vimala), Candrabhāsa (= Candrajñāna), Vīraja (= Vīra), Saurabheya (= Vātula); the Śrīkaṇṭhīya puts Maukuṭa among the Śivabhedas and has Madgīta, Nārasiṃha, Candrāṃśu, Vīrabhadra, Visara, Vimala and Saurabheya among the Rudrabhedas. Scholarly note: most titles survive, if at all, as later South Indian ritual redactions; early texts survive for the Niśvāsa, Kiraṇa, Svāyambhuva and Raurava (sūtrasaṅgrahas) and some upāgamas.

definitions.definition: Ten Śivabheda and eighteen Rudrabheda root scriptures of the upper stream, each revealed to a Śiva or Rudra and handed down; they are the limbs of Sadāśiva's mantra-body.
The 'ten' and 'eighteen' of Śiva's teaching, whose essence is the Trika (TĀ 1.18).

name: The upāgamas (upabhedas) of the Siddhānta
members: Mṛgendra (classed under the Kāmika by tradition)
Kālajñāna / Uttara (Vātula; cf. the Kālottara corpus)
notes: Only the better-known upāgamas are listed here; the full per-Āgama lists are in the structure.upabhedas_kamika field of each src entry.

definitions.definition: Subsidiary scriptures attached to the 28 root Āgamas; the Kāmika names them one by one (206 by its stated counts; tradition usually says 207); the Kiraṇa calls any division within a division an upabheda and says the divisions differ in knowledge, not in fruit.

name: The descent of the tantras (tantrāvatāra)

definitions.definition: Right after creation Śiva divided the one knowledge among ten Śivas and eighteen Rudras, each text then passing through a chain of recipients (a Śiva/Rudra, then gods, sages or gaṇas) to reach humans.

name: The Āgamas as the body of Sadāśiva

relations.note: both treat a sacred whole as the Lord's body

definitions.definition: The 28 tantras are the limbs of Sadāśiva's body made of tantras and mantras, from the Kāmika as his feet to the Vātula as his garment; one scripture, manifold through the hearers.

name: The four pādas of an Āgama

relations.note: the Tamil Siddhānta reads caryā-kriyā-yoga-jñāna as ascending stages (U18/U51)

notes: Scholarly note: the neat fourfold arrangement is an ideal that many surviving texts do not follow.

definitions.definition: Knowledge (vidyā/jñāna), ritual (kriyā), yoga and conduct (caryā); all of Śiva's scriptures are said to have them and to serve enjoyment and liberation.
The Pādma Saṃhitā is arranged in the four pādas jñāna, yoga, kriyā, caryā.

name: Higher and lower knowledge (para/apara jñāna) in the Āgamas

relations.note: Pāñcarātrins and Vaikhānasas claim Vedic roots instead

definitions.definition: Knowledge is twofold by eligibility: Śiva's knowledge, revealing the Lord, is higher; the Veda and the rest, revealing the bound soul and its bonds, are lower — different as the night-vision of a man and a cat.

name: Āgama as rooted in or continuous with the Veda
notes: Bhāskararāya's statement read in the local Setubandha e-text; no teaching id created (U23).

definitions.definition: The Pāñcarātra is the Lord's own word and of Vedic root; its followers are brahmins.
Vaikhānasa worship follows the path of the śruti in every rite and is performed with Vedic mantras.
Tantras that teach the worship of Rāma, Kṛṣṇa, Nṛsiṃha, Rudra, Paraśiva or Sundarī are rooted in Upaniṣads such as the Rāmatāpanī and are beyond doubt (Bhāskararāya, Setubandha introduction).

name: Enjoyment and liberation as the twofold goal (bhukti-mukti)

definitions.definition: Śiva's scriptures in all four pādas are means to enjoyment (powers, higher worlds) and to liberation; initiates are bubhukṣu or mumukṣu accordingly.

name: The grades of Śaiva initiates
notes: Standard in Siddhānta paddhatis (e.g. Somaśambhu); no verse-level teaching recorded in this pass.

definitions.definition: Samayin (after samaya-dīkṣā), putraka (after nirvāṇa-dīkṣā, seeking liberation), sādhaka (consecrated to master a mantra for powers) and ācārya/deśika (consecrated teacher who may initiate and install).

name: Kinds of initiation (dīkṣā) in the Āgamas

definitions.definition: Initiation acts on the soul, not caste or body; it is the cause of the other means and, as nirvāṇa-dīkṣā, destroys past and future karma through mantra-power, the present body continuing like a potter's wheel. It is samaya- (or viśeṣa-) and nirvāṇa-dīkṣā, followed by consecrations (abhiṣeka) of sādhaka and ācārya; for the incapable the observances are purified away ('seedless', nirbīja), for the capable they remain ('with seed').
Initiation (dīkṣā) into Bhagavān's mantras and worship; in Śrīvaiṣṇava usage the five sacraments.

name: Descent of power / grace (śaktipāta)

relations.note: Both lineages use the one term for the Lord's grace and both link it to karmasāmya; they differ on direction (Kiraṇa: equality marks the time of descent; Ahirbudhnya: the Lord's glance brings about equality).
the Kiraṇa's śaktipāta chapter leads directly into its dīkṣā chapter

definitions.definition: Śiva's awakening of the soul by his power, spoken of figuratively as a 'fall'; it occurs at the time of the equality of karma, Śiva remaining its lord as the sun is of the lotus; its sign is a distinctive devotion.
Viṣṇu's compassion, his fifth power of grace, which āgama-knowers call śaktipāta: by his glance the soul's karmas become equal and fall silent, and it is lifted from saṃsāra.

name: Grace (anugraha) as the Lord's fifth act
notes: U18/U19 record Śiva's five acts; this is the Pāñcarātra contribution.

definitions.definition: Grace is the last of Lakṣmī's (the Lord's) five acts — concealment, creation, maintenance, dissolution, grace.

name: Signs of the descent of power and of freedom from bonds

definitions.definition: A distinctive devotion (bhakti) marks the descent of power; in one freed from bonds by initiation the sign is steadiness of disposition and absence of wavering in the prescribed action, though signs are not always evident.

name: Powers (siddhi) and the sādhaka in the Mantramārga
notes: The Vidyāpīṭha's observance (vidyāvrata) is recorded in summary only (restricted).

definitions.definition: The sādhaka masters a mantra through observances to gain powers and enjoyments; for the yogin striving in the limbs of yoga, powers shine forth like the sun's rays and no being can overpower him.

name: The Lord, the bound soul and its bonds (pati, paśu, pāśa)
notes: Contribution from U08; U18 owns the Siddhānta concept.

definitions.definition: The Kiraṇa teaches the knowledge of paśu, pāśa and pati; the soul is eternal, pervasive, ignorant and inactive, lodged within māyā and bound through kalā, vidyā, rāga, prakṛti and the instruments.

name: The sixty-four Bhairava tantras
members: Bhairavāṣṭaka: Svacchanda, Bhairava, Caṇḍa, Krodha, Unmatta, Asitāṅga, Mahocchuṣma, Kapālīśa
Yāmalāṣṭaka: Brahma-, Viṣṇu-, Svacchanda-, Ruru-, (5th unnamed), Ātharvaṇa-, Rudra-, Vetāla-yāmala
Matāṣṭaka: Rakta, Lampaṭa, Lakṣmīmata, (Mata?), Cālikā, Piṅgala, Utphullaka, Viśvādya
Maṅgalāṣṭaka: Bhairavī (Picu, twofold), (3rd unnamed), Brāhmī Kalā, Vijayā, Candrā, Maṅgalā, Sarvamaṅgalā
Cakrāṣṭaka: Mantra-, Varṇa-, Śakti-, Kalā-, Bindu-, Nāda-, Guhya-, Kha-cakra
Bahurūpāṣṭaka: Andhaka, Rurubheda, Aja, Mūla, Varṇabhaṇṭha, Viḍaṅga, Jvālin, Mātṛrodana
Vāgīśāṣṭaka: Bhairavī, Citrikā, Haṃsā, Kadambikā, Hṛllekhā, Candralekhā, Vidyullekhā, Vidyumān
Śikhāṣṭaka: Bhairavī Śikhā, Vīṇā, Vīṇāmaṇi, Sammoha, Ḍāmara, Atharvaka, Kabandha, Śiraścheda
notes: Checked against Jayaratha's quotation in the local Tantrāloka e-text; three slots are unnamed or unclear in the quoted text. Surviving texts include the Svacchanda (1), Brahmayāmala (2), Jayadrathayāmala (= Śiraścheda, 8); the Vīṇāśikha and Sammoha belong to the Vāma stream.

definitions.definition: The Śrīkaṇṭhīya's eight groups of eight (Bhairava, Yāmala, Mata, Maṅgala, Cakra, Bahurūpa, Vāgīśa, Śikhā), each group 'spoken' by one of the Bhairavas; together 'the wheel of Sadāśiva'.
The 'eight times eight' of Śiva's teaching, dominated by non-duality.

name: Śiva-, Rudra- and Bhairava-tantras as teaching difference, difference-in-identity and non-difference

relations.note: the Saiddhāntikas read their scriptures as teaching the soul's distinctness and reject this ranking (see dsp:rank-of-siddhanta-and-bhairava-tantras)

definitions.definition: Jayaratha derives the ten Śiva-tantras (difference), eighteen Rudra-tantras (difference-and-non-difference) and sixty-four Bhairava-tantras (non-duality) from the combinations of Sadāśiva's faces: knowledge itself unfolds in these three ways.

name: Worship for oneself and worship for others

definitions.definition: Worship is twofold: for oneself, in the liṅga received at initiation or on a ground-altar, for one's own fruit; for others, in temples with installed liṅgas, for the king and realm.

name: Kinds of liṅga

definitions.definition: Self-manifest (svayambhu), divine (daiva), bāṇa, sages' (ārṣa) and man-installed liṅgas are the supports of temple worship; the liṅga given by the guru is the support of one's own worship.

name: The five purifications (pañcaśuddhi)

definitions.definition: Before worship: purification of oneself, of the place, of the substances, of the mantras and of the liṅga.

name: The six paths (ṣaḍadhvan)
notes: No verse-level anchor recorded in this pass.

definitions.definition: The cosmos as six 'paths' — letters (varṇa), words (pada), mantras, kalās, principles (tattva) and worlds (bhuvana) — traversed and purified in nirvāṇa-dīkṣā.

name: The five kalās

definitions.definition: Nivṛtti, pratiṣṭhā, vidyā, śānti and śāntyatīta, the five enclosing divisions of the principles, purified in initiation.

name: The temple as the deity's body
notes: Stated in many texts; exact loci not verified in this pass (listed as a gap). U58 owns Vāstu/Śilpa.

definitions.definition: Āgama and śilpa texts treat the temple (prāsāda) as the body of the deity, its parts named as limbs.
Pāñcarātra saṃhitās likewise identify the temple with Bhagavān's body.
Kerala tantra treats the temple and its installed deity as a living body whose power the tantri maintains.

name: Installation (pratiṣṭhā): making the deity present

definitions.definition: The series of rites from ploughing the site to installation, performed with a single root āgama; by it the deity is established in liṅga or image.
The fixed and movable images are installed and linked; the fixed stands for the partless, the movable for the partite form.
Installation of the seven deities, reserved to the tantri.

name: The six qualities of Bhagavān (ṣāḍguṇya)

relations.note: the six are 'aprākṛta'; the Lord is nirguṇa with respect to prakṛti's three guṇas

definitions.definition: Knowledge, power, lordship, strength, virility and splendour; knowledge is Brahman's very form and the other five its aspects; the six are also Lakṣmī's body; pairs of them manifest as the vyūhas.

name: The four vyūhas

definitions.definition: Vāsudeva, Saṅkarṣaṇa (knowledge and strength), Pradyumna (lordship and virility) and Aniruddha (power and splendour), each nonetheless possessing all six qualities.
As reported by Śaṅkara: Vāsudeva the highest Self, Saṅkarṣaṇa the soul, Pradyumna mind, Aniruddha ego-sense — a doctrine of the soul's origination he rejects.

name: The five modes of God: para, vyūha, vibhava, antaryāmin, arcā
notes: The fivefold list is standard in Pāñcarātra and Śrīvaiṣṇava writing; a single verse stating all five is not anchored here. U14 records the Viśiṣṭādvaita version.

definitions.definition: Bhagavān exists as the supreme (para), the emanations (vyūha), the descents (vibhava), the inner controller (antaryāmin) and the consecrated image (arcā).

name: The thirty-nine vibhavas
notes: Forty names result if every epithet is counted separately; the text says thirty-nine (segmentation uncertain).

definitions.definition: The Lord's descents beginning with Padmanābha and ending with Pātālaśayana, whose details the Sātvata teaches.

name: Pure and other-than-pure creation

definitions.definition: Creation proceeds from the Lord's Śakti as a pure creation (the vyūhas from pairs of qualities) and an other-than-pure creation from prakṛti; the Jayākhya orders the Vaiṣṇava (pure), primordial-matter and Brahmā's creations.

name: Lakṣmī as Nārāyaṇa's Śakti

definitions.definition: Śrī is Nārāyaṇa's eternal, independent power whose body is the six qualities, who performs his five acts, and in whom one takes refuge.

name: The five acts in the Pāñcarātra

relations.note: same five functions, differently ordered; the Śaiva list is recorded by U18/U19

definitions.definition: Concealment, creation, maintenance, dissolution and grace, performed by Śrī as Nārāyaṇa's power.

name: The six limbs of surrender (ṣaḍaṅga śaraṇāgati)

definitions.definition: Resolve to do what pleases, avoidance of what displeases, faith that he will protect, choosing him as protector, laying down oneself, helplessness.

name: The qualified recipient of the tantra

definitions.definition: One who does not revile scripture, has faith and devotion to Lakṣmī and Nārāyaṇa, and knows ritual, other tantras, yoga, Veda and Vedāṅga, Paśupati's doctrine, logic and all spiritual śāstras.
Those fit for ritual, knowledge or conduct are joined to Śiva accordingly; the incapable receive initiation without the observances.

name: The three gems of the Pāñcarātra and their expansions

definitions.definition: Sātvata, Pauṣkara and Jayākhya issue directly from the Lord; their expansions Īśvara, Pārameśvara and Pādma govern practice at Melkote, Śrīraṅgam and Kāñcī respectively.

name: The 108 Pāñcarātra saṃhitās
notes: Scholarly metadata: F. O. Schrader (1916) combined several saṃhitās' lists into over 200 titles; many titles are lost. Members are the src entries with lineage lin:pancaratra.

definitions.definition: Tradition speaks of 108 saṃhitās spoken by the Lord; lists of titles in different saṃhitās disagree.

name: The four siddhāntas of the Pāñcarātra

definitions.definition: Mantra-siddhānta (one form predominant), Āgama-siddhānta (four forms), Tantra-siddhānta (nine forms) and Tantrāntara (a four- or three-faced deity).

name: The five periods of the day (pañcakāla)

definitions.definition: The Pāñcarātrin's day is ordered as approach, gathering, worship, study and yoga.

name: Viṣṇu partless and with parts (Vaikhānasa)

relations.note: both link degrees of the divine form to kinds of worship; neither tradition equates the schemes

definitions.definition: The supreme Brahman Nārāyaṇa has a subtle, imperishable, partless form, stood for by the fixed image, and a gross form with parts, cause of all, stood for by the movable image that receives full worship.

name: The five forms of Viṣṇu (Vaikhānasa)

definitions.definition: Viṣṇu, Puruṣa, Satya, Acyuta and Aniruddha, invoked in worship (Puruṣa, Satya, Acyuta, Aniruddha placed in the directions).

name: The five images (pañcabera)

definitions.definition: Fixed (dhruva), worship (kautuka), festival (utsava), bathing (snapana) and offering (bali) images; the dhruva receives flowers only, the kautuka full worship.

name: Formless and embodied worship (amūrta / samūrta)

definitions.definition: Worship of Viṣṇu is through the fire without form, or in a consecrated image; image worship is praised as best.

name: Vaiṣṇava from the womb (garbha-vaiṣṇava)

relations.note: the two communities disagree on whether branding is required

definitions.definition: Through the prenatal viṣṇubali the Vaikhānasa is a Vaiṣṇava before birth and does not take the branding initiation.
The five sacraments, beginning with branding, make one a Vaiṣṇava.

name: Four forms of liberation in the Vaikhānasa tradition
notes: Recalled from Vaikhānasa literature (Vimānārcanakalpa); correlation of these with particular means is not recorded here (unverified).

definitions.definition: Attaining Viṣṇu's world (sālokya), nearness (sāmīpya), likeness of form (sārūpya) and union (sāyujya).

name: The seven deities of the Tantrasamuccaya

definitions.definition: Viṣṇu, Śiva, Śaṅkaranārāyaṇa, Durgā, Subrahmaṇya, Gaṇapati and Śāstā, whose installation and worship the Tantrasamuccaya prescribes.

name: The tantri and the śānti in Kerala temples

definitions.definition: A hereditary tantri family holds ritual authority over a temple (installation, festivals, purifications), while śānti priests perform the daily pūjās; e.g. the Cēnnās family at Guruvāyūr.

name: The sixty-four tantras of the Śākta lists

relations.note: different lists of 'sixty-four', overlapping only partly (e.g. Kāmika, Vātula, Candrajñāna and Sarvajñānottara appear here, Siddhānta titles in the Śaiva lists)

definitions.definition: The Vāmakeśvara's sixty-four tantras 'of the Mothers' (Mahāmāyā, Śambara … Viśuddheśvara), by which, the Saundaryalaharī says, Paśupati beguiled the world before revealing the Goddess's own tantra; Lakṣmīdhara judges them Kaula and non-Vedic.

name: The five auspicious āgamas and the Samaya way

definitions.definition: Lakṣmīdhara's Vedic Samaya canon — the Vasiṣṭha, Sanaka, Śuka, Sanandana and Sanatkumāra saṃhitās — opposed to the 'mixed' Candrakalā group and the Kaula sixty-four.

name: The three krāntās (Viṣṇukrāntā, Rathakrāntā, Aśvakrāntā)
notes: From memory; not verified. Owner of doctrine: U24.

definitions.definition: A later Śākta division of India into three regions, each with its own sixty-four tantras (192 in all), recorded in texts such as the Mahāsiddhasāra.
